pairs.evidence: src/features/agents/AGENTS.md:67 The nested instruction file tells agents this context's tool runner lives inside a chat turn, while its only production mount is the Design Connectors sub-tab (DesignSubtabPanels.tsx:121) and the module contains no mention of chat, so the trusted layer misplaces the surface.

techniques.evidence: src/features/agents/AGENTS.md:67 Stale row: rg finds ToolRunnerPanel and ToolInvocationCard used outside the module only by DesignSubtabPanels and its test; rg -i chat in sub_tool_runner returns nothing. The row also disagrees with line 56, which puts the tool runner in the design tab. The boundary gate checks row names only, so it stays green.

src/features/agents/AGENTS.md:14 The file names the gate instead of restating the rule, and the gate operates: the script exits 0 reporting 16 modules, 19 pairs and 26 imports, and agents-sub-boundaries.test.ts asserts compare() returns no problems.

src/features/agents/AGENTS.md:69 Lines 69-74 keep a history of removed rows while line 70 says the check now catches a stale row; the technique says a rule whose failure mode a gate now catches is removed, not kept as residue.

pairs.registryProposal: A row-presence gate over an ownership table can certify a table whose descriptions are stale. enforcement-demotion could name this proxy case explicitly: the gate fires and is real, yet it covers only the row key.
